notes:
Summary: Northbridge is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for low-latency FIN/HT trading assistant + high-volume embeddings for compliance search. Key ask is deterministic throughput guarantees with regional failover and clear SLA credits.

Requirements / what they told us: - 1000 concurrent chat sessions at p99 <= 30ms for short-turn responses; typical seq len 128 tokens. - Embedding pipeline: sustained 40k documents/hour with p95 < 200ms per embed. - Reranking endpoint: bursty traffic up to 8k QPS during market open, needs reserved headroom. - Preferred reserved hardware: H100 for chat (latency) and A100 for large-batch embeddings.

Multi-region reserved pool ask: - Primary region (us-east-1): reserve 40 GPUs (mix H100/A100) to meet baseline. - DR region (us-west-2): reserve 12 GPUs as hot standby for failover (30% headroom). - EU region (eu-west-1): reserve 18 GPUs for EU-resident workloads and data residency. - Cross-region failover plan: automated routing with warm KV cache pre-warming for last-active sessions; expected cold-start penalty tolerable up to 150ms for degraded mode.

Operational constraints / preferences: - Want dedicated capacity to have guaranteed per-GPU throughput metrics and an isolation SLA. - Need autoscaling burst pool to handle market-open spikes; prefer burst to be charged separately with cap. - Ask for canary rollout and model pinning during trading hours to avoid regressions. - Require audit logging, KMS integration, and monthly usage breakdown by token and latency buckets.

Commercial / SLA negotiation notes: - Interested in a 12-month reserved contract with quarterly review. - Asking for SLO credit structure: 5% credit for monthly availability < 99.95%, tiered for larger breaches. - Procurement flagged multi-region budget; wants clear uplift premium per region.

Quotes / verbatim: - "We need the headroom plan nailed down before trading pilot." - "If failover adds more than 100ms p99, we cannot use it for front-office flows."
